title: Paystride Payroll Card Program Restoration Reserve and Restoring Payment Worksheet
content:
## Purpose of the reserve figure

When the desk works out a restoring payment for a Paystride Payroll Card Program, and only then, the reserve the funding balance must hold is the restoration reserve; for every other purpose the reserve remains under the reserve rule, which reads: After each regular batch the funding balance must still hold the package's reserve percent of the average of the program's most recent regular batches.

## Calculation

**A. Restoration look-back.** The restoration look-back holds the funding entries dated today or earlier that lie fewer than three whole months before today, the whole months between two dates being the difference in calendar months less one when the later date's day of the month is smaller than the earlier date's.

**B. Restoration batch basis.** The restoration batch basis is the average regular batch: the amounts of the regular payroll batches posted in the restoration look-back summed and divided by their number, or zero when none posted.

**C. Restoration reserve.** The restoration reserve is the package's reserve percent, taken as a number of percent, of the restoration batch basis, and it is rounded half up to the cent. The order of the figures is fixed: the figure taken as the restoration batch basis is settled first, multipliers of the restoration batch basis are applied to it next, amounts added to the restoration batch basis are added after that, and the percentage and the multipliers of the restoration reserve are applied to that result last, before the rounding.

**D. Restoring payment.** The restoring payment is the restoration reserve less the funding balance, and is zero when the funding balance already holds the restoration reserve.

## Look-back boundary (hypothetical, today being 15 May)

| Entry dated | Whole months before today | In the look-back |
|---|---|---|
| 15 May | 0 | yes |
| 16 February | 2 | yes |
| 15 February | 3 | no |

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

A hypothetical Select package program (reserve percent 5) has four regular payroll batches posted in the look-back, of 15,210.40, 16,004.75, 14,889.10 and 15,731.95.

1. Restoration batch basis: 61,836.20 divided by 4, that is 15,459.05.
2. Restoration reserve: 5 percent of 15,459.05 is 772.9525, rounded half up to 772.95.
3. With a funding balance of minus 214.60, the restoring payment is 772.95 less minus 214.60, that is 987.55.
4. With a funding balance of 800.00 the balance already holds the reserve, and the restoring payment is zero.
